summary: An educational 3D animated storytelling series, interactive digital hub, and written research project created by Asia Tarannum (Space Ornament Team) for school-age children. It brings to life the overlooked, pioneering missions of Snoopy (Apollo 10), Mariner 4, Mariner 9, and Viking 1, inspiring young learners with the untold history of Moon and Mars exploration.
details:
What is this project?
"Space Ornaments: Forgotten Stories of NASA Space Probes of the Moon and Mars" is a multimedia educational project designed to teach school-age children about the unsung robotic heroes of space exploration. Just as precious ornaments adorn what we treasure, NASA’s early space probes are the true "Space Ornaments" of our solar system—standing as enduring symbols of human curiosity, ingenuity, and presence beyond Earth.
Hosted by an animated 3D avatar of creator Asia Tarannum, this project tells the first-person stories of four legendary NASA spacecraft:
• Snoopy (Apollo 10 Lunar Module): The brave lunar dress rehearsal that flew within 15.6 km of the Moon to ensure Apollo 11 could land safely.
• Mariner 4: The first spacecraft to successfully fly past Mars and capture the very first 22 close-up photographs of another planet.
• Mariner 9: The first spacecraft to orbit another planet, braving a massive global dust storm to map 85% of Mars and discover Olympus Mons.

• Viking 1: The first spacecraft to successfully land on Mars, sending back the first color surface photos and operating for over six years.

How does it work? (Three-Part Learning Model)
Specially designed for school-age children, this project combines three integrated components:
1. 3D Pixar-Style Animated Video Series: Child-friendly, first-person animated episodes with expressive voiceovers and emotional storytelling.
2. Interactive Digital Hub: A centralized digital document linking all animated episodes, mission timelines, and written chapters in one place.
3. Written Research Assignment: A structured, fact-checked written companion detailing launch dates, scientific discoveries, and real NASA data for deeper study.
